name: Schema Validator
title: Schema Validator: Test JSON-LD Against Google's Rules
description: Free schema validator: parse every JSON-LD block on a URL and flag syntax errors and missing required properties per Google's structured data docs.
answer: A schema validator checks a page's structured data in two layers: is the JSON-LD valid, and does it meet Google's requirements for the rich result it targets? Enter a URL to find every schema type on the page, see missing required and recommended properties, and spot types Google has retired.
trust: We parse every JSON-LD block in the live HTML and check each type against the property rules in Google's current structured data documentation.
body:
## Schema Markup Validator: Syntax vs Google Eligibility

Two different questions, two different tools. The [Schema Markup Validator](https://validator.schema.org/) checks that markup is valid schema.org; Google's [Rich Results Test](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results) checks whether it qualifies for a Google feature. Valid schema can still be ineligible — a Product without offers, reviews or ratings gets no product snippet.

This validator does both in one pass: syntax errors first, then Google's required and recommended properties for each type.

## Schema Checker: Find Every Type on a Page

Pages often carry more markup than their owners know — a theme adds Organization, a plugin adds BreadcrumbList, an old template adds FAQPage. We list every type found in every JSON-LD block, nested ones included.

## Structured Data Testing Tool: The Replacement for Google's

Google retired its Structured Data Testing Tool and [moved schema validation to schema.org](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2020/12/structured-data-testing-tool-update), pointing site owners to the Rich Results Test for Google features. This page covers the same ground for any public URL, with Google's rules applied per type.

## Schema Markup Checker for Product, FAQ, Article and More

Rules come from Google's [search gallery](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/search-gallery) documentation: Article, Product, Offer, Review, AggregateRating, BreadcrumbList, Event, JobPosting, LocalBusiness, Recipe, SoftwareApplication, VideoObject, Organization and more.

Retired types are flagged instead of passed. Google stopped showing FAQ rich results on May 7, 2026, and HowTo, Course info and several others earlier ([Search Central updates](https://developers.google.com/search/updates)). Yet when we analyzed 315 big-brand homepages in October 2026 ([dataset](/resources/technical-seo-baseline-2026-10.json)), 11.1% still carried FAQPage markup — harmless, but no longer earning anything in Google.

## Does valid schema guarantee rich results?

No. Google states plainly that it [doesn't guarantee](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/sd-policies) structured data will show up even when it's correct. Content quality, policy compliance and the query all matter. JSON-LD is Google's recommended format ([Google](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data)), and 74% of the homepages in our sample used it.

Then check which result types a page can win with the [rich snippets test](/tools/rich-snippets-test), or generate clean markup with the [schema generator](/tools/schema-generator).

faqs.q: What is the best schema validator?
faqs.a: Use two checks: the Schema Markup Validator for schema.org syntax and Google's Rich Results Test for Google eligibility. This tool combines both views for any public URL.

faqs.q: Is FAQ schema still worth adding?
faqs.a: Not for Google rich results: Google stopped showing FAQ rich results on May 7, 2026. The markup is harmless and can still help other systems read your Q&A, but don't expect a SERP feature.

faqs.q: JSON-LD, Microdata or RDFa — which should I use?
faqs.a: Google says all three are fine when valid, and recommends JSON-LD because it is the easiest to add and maintain. This tool reads JSON-LD.

faqs.q: Why does Google ignore my valid structured data?
faqs.a: Google never guarantees rich results. Markup can be ignored if it describes content users can't see, breaks a policy, or the page isn't considered helpful enough for the feature.
